title: Recording with Woody Herman in New York, 1944
summary: On vacation he subbed for Cliff Leeman with Woody Herman and recorded Perdido and other sides.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, were you there constantly or were you off sometimes?
No, I was there most all of the time. And -- but I had such a good relationship with the proprietor.
I would think so. You were there 21 years.

Yeah, right, right. And I had such a good relation with him that -- I would take my vacation, I could put somebody in my place, and then, like I said, during the war, Woody Herman's band -- Woody came to me and this was with Dave Tough and Cliff Leeman.
Right, right, I recorded some things with him, yeah, right.
"Perdido" was one of them. "The Music Stopped," Ben Webster was on the thing, right. Johnny Hodges, yeah, right, right. And T'zol, Juan Tizol.*
Yeah, (inaudible) "Down in Basie's Basement", is that --
No, I didn't do that one. But this --
right. I don't remember all of the sides, but these are a few of them.

No, we did it in New York, see. Now, I was -- like I told you, I was vacationing in New York, and Cliff at that time, well, he was getting ready to go to the Army, and he was -- so I worked in his place. And then later --
Did you work with the band?
